newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels free small group of hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels free small group of hostages.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist rebels holding VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima freed at least three more captives on Saturday.

The release came shortly after the Peruvian government's chief negotiator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo, spent three hours and 15 minutes inside the fortified compound, in what was the first visit of a government official inside the residence since the siege began.

Two of the freed hostages seen coming out of the residence on live television were recognized by witnesses as the Dominican Republic ambassador, Jose Diaz, and the President of the Peruvian Association of Exporters, Enrique Pendavis.
The three men left the building with Michel Minnig of the Red Cross -- the official mediator in the crisis.
The latest release meant the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels were holding 100 VIP hostages in the residence.
